notes.title: Small steam update
notes.content:
Hello Planimal trainers, as our promise to keep you all updated, we've just launched a small update with various fixes. In addition to this, the demo on our steam page has been updated to reflect the fixes from QOL 1 & 2.

Switch has also been brought up to parity, with the PC version which you can read about [url=https://www.mergegames.com/news/monster-harvest-switch-update/]here.[/url]

notes.title: QOL2 launch date + features expanded
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

With QOL2 coming to PC [b]this Thursday the 15th[/b], its filled with some new additions and bug fixes that you can [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1363350/view/3316360267002942860]check out in our last post[/url]. 

Below are some of the new features being shipped with the update:

[u]Introducing Aster & The Clothing Store[/u]
[i]A new merchant arrives in town.[/i]
- Change your character to 1 of 32 appearances
- Aster can be romanced and gifted, the conclusion resulting in a reward cutscene
- Shop visuals also improved

[u]Combat 2.0[/u]
[i]New options to turn the tide in your favour[/i]
- Escape Battle option now available
- Swap Planimals mid-battle
- Heal Planimals between battles with potions bought from the clinic

[u]House Customization[/u]
[i]Time for a facelift[/i]
- 5 different house styles available to purchase from the sign outside the player house
- Cosmetic changes persist across house levels. 

[u]Festival Improvements[/u]
[i]My fish is bigger than yours![/i]
- Livestock festival will trigger a cutscene after 90 seconds of being at the festival
- Fishing contest allows the player to submit a fish for judging
- The cookoff allows players to enter a dish of their choice to be scrutinized

notes.title: Holiday Update
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

First off, as we have said numerous times now, [b]thank you for the feedback[/b] that’s been shared since the beta through to launch and beyond, it shapes the way we develop and build the game.

After the post-launch flurry of updates, things have been a little quieter, which isn’t ideal. We really want to provide you with meaningful updates which we couldn't do until the [b]initial bug fixing patches[/b] were completed and work progressed on the more quality of life focused update which was promised.

We’re a small team but we’re passionate about what we do and giving you an enjoyable gaming experience is really what we sign up for by coming to work in the games industry. We know there have been frustrations out there and despite things being quieter on the communication front, we’ve certainly tried to give every player a voice, hear your concerns and take them to heart. We don’t want to overpromise on something until we’re sure of it, so a lot of Monster Harvest has been behind the scenes work lately.

With that said, we’re in a position now to share details on the [b]next updates for Monster Harvest[/b]! These will come in the form of 2 updates, for all platforms.

[u][b]Update 1[/b][/u]
Coming early in the new year! It will land on PC first, followed by consoles which require some additional porting and certification before we can get them out to you.

[b]Massive UI overhaul[/b]
[list]
[*] Menus all optimized and some redesigned
 [*] Text popups for pickups and items
 [*] Rescaled multiple text instance
[/list]
[b]- Controller support improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Improving controls & menu navigation when using a controller
[/list]
[b]- Crop signposting[/b]
[list]
[*] Crops will now more clearly tell you when they are ready to harvest
[/list]
[b]- A map of Planimal Point is now available[/b]

[b]- See where you stand with the resident of Planimal Point with a new relationship tracker[/b]

notes.title: Monster Harvest Launch... and beyond
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/694694ca338cea97e9d8012f9b6e78a33b217e2a.png[/img]
Hey everyone,

Today is the day many have been waiting for, Planimal Point is open!

It's been quite a ride getting here. Monster Harvest began, honestly, as quite a small project. The core concept of the game has always been a [b]unique twist on the genre[/b], but the more we showed the game to people, the more expectations grew and we adjusted the scope of the project to align better with those rising expectations. 

Hence Monster Harvest was delayed a number of times whilst we worked on expanding the scope of the game and working in features requested by the growing community, feedback from early beta testing and realising further ambitions for just what Monster Harvest could be. Building upon a concept is a road lined with pitfalls, and this is why we took the increasingly harder decision to delay rather than try to rush out with features packed in without doing the necessary testing.

notes.title: Characters & Seasons
notes.content:
Hi Everyone! 

Today we have bit of a two-for-one post about seasons in the game and also the playable characters.

First up we have the main character, originally we only had the character seen in the trailers but due to popular demand we've expanded that roster to four playable characters. We understand that player's want a character that resembles themselves to really immerse themselves in the world, so we hope you enjoy the ones we've come up with below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/fad5ab1573692a5bc5104d8d9762364974c2867f.gif[/img]

We pride ourselves on empowering the player to play however they want, so when overwhelming feedback came in for more characters we just couldn't resist! Do you think we should add even more? Let us know what you'd like to see and it could make a great update!

Next up is the seasons. We wanted to give the player a new experience and went back to the drawing board to see if we could improve one of the fundamental core features of the farming genre.

Typically, farming games will have North American style seasons of Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. But we've all played that before right? So isn't there anything else we can do? Well a lot of the real world is broken up into wet and dry seasons and we thought that would be a great place to start. We wanted to add variety as well so we added a third season into the mix known as the dark season. And on top of that we shortened the seasons down to 21 days a piece, instead of the genre standard of 28, so player's can see more in less time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/f89eebcb990450faf9947fe5644dc4be34026898.gif[/img]

We found that having three extremely visually distinct seasons really added to the mystery and flavor of the game and made the experience unique.

This game was made to be charming, surprising, fun, and customizable and so the seasons are no different. We hope you have enjoyed this post and we look forward to your feedback!

notes.title: The Story of Monster Harvest
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

So you know how to use slime, and super slime, to mutate a whole range of crops. The question is, why are you in Planimal Point? Here's an overview of how slimes fit into the story of Monster Harvest, and their significance to the town of Planimal Point

The world of Monster Harvest takes place in a new town called Planimal Point. The town has popped up around the discovery of Slimes (which we talked about in our last blog). We were inspired by gold rush style towns that popped up in California and the Yukon where people would rush to get in on the start of new communities. These town's were hapharzardly built and we wanted to reflect that look in the game.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/2iyaWxa.gif[/img]

Slimes are a magical and semi-conscious substance that has strange effects on plant life. Different Slimes can mutate plants into different creatures or even more exotic versions of plants. Planimals can be used to help the player battle enemies in dungeons but some mutations will produce livestock and even mounts to ride around on. The player's uncle, Professor Spark, discovered the Slimes and his lab is right in the center of town.

A lot of people have come to Planimal Point and for different reasons. Many have come to open shops and start new lives, but one has come to exploit the Slimes. Rigley works for the evil SlimeCo. Pumping, a company looking to take advantage of Slimes for nefarious purposes...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/89OzC6m.gif[/img]

In order to stop SlimeCo. the player must delve deep into the dungeon with the help of their Planimals!

notes.title: Slime Mechanics
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We want to talk you through some of the slime mechanics in the game, where you can 

The big thing we wanted to focus on when creating Monster Harvest was to create a system for mutating crops. We came up with the Slime system, a system that allows players to mutate each crop in 6 unique ways. Right now, there are 12 crops (some which can only be found in dungeons) and so there are 72 mutations so far!

Thanks to your trusty 'plantdex' you'll soon discover what each mutation makes and learn how to best optimize your farm. There are three base Slimes, and three 'Super Slimes'. Slimes are easily applied to crops and once the crop has completed growing it will emerge as a mutation.

Base slimes are pretty common and can be found even outside of the dungeon. They come in red, blue, and green. Red Slimes make Planimals which are best for protecting the player and battling enemies. Blue Slimes make livestock which the player can keep in their barn. Green Slimes accelerate growth, and I mean really accelerate it, in fact it gives you the final crop instantly (think of this one as a super fertilizer).

Below we have the first crop given to the player - the Mutato (mutant potato!). You'll see it can make the Mutanko Planimal, the Mutabbit livestock, or instant growth. For the Livestock you'll still have to wait for the baby to grow to an adult so make sure you feed them every day!

notes.title: Developer's Blog 3 - Code Complete!
notes.content:
Hi Everyone!

Looks like people are really enjoying the 2.5D conversion so thanks for reading that last post and giving us the push we needed to move the game in such a cool direction :)

You’ll be pleased to hear that we've locked in our final code and are just hunting down the last few bugs and adjusting the games 'feel'. Game feel can be notoriously hard to nail down but I think we have it figured out.

There are a range of little things that contribute to game feel such as player speed, tool usage, and even the clock. Time in the game was changed from a ticking clock to a constant day or night to make the game a relaxing and fun adventure. We thought it would be better to limit the player only with stamina, so you could stop and smell the roses and not feel any kind of time crunch while playing.

We've also added so much to the game that we think everyone will really enjoy. We've added fishing, decorating, and even a tournament at the rec centre where you can battle everyone in town! Fishing especially is my favourite activity and comes with a great microgame as you try to reel them in.

Thanks everyone - we'll keep you updated as we continue towards the game's release. It's been a blast working on it and we really hope you enjoy how everything has come together!

The last blog focused on what inspired us to create a pixel art game and how Monster Harvest is built using Unity meaning it isn’t purely a 2D game, but a 3D render with the camera locked to a 90-degree angle aiming at the world. 

(If you missed that blog, you can read it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1363350/announcements/detail/2968402022832253006]here[/url] )

That got us thinking though…. What could the game look like if we toyed around with the camera angle?

So, we did a bit of messing around and started developing how the game could look in a 2.5D style, keeping all the art the same, but making it so the characters, trees, buildings, and all other objects in the world stick up, like a pop-up book.

Well after a lot of prototyping, testing, and a sneak peek in a [url=https://twitter.com/mergegamesltd?lang=he]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.com/mergegames]Discord[/url] Poll to see what you guys and gals preferred (thanks to everyone who voted!), we’ve now converted most of the game to 2.5D! 

Check out how the game is looking now: 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/395eb3db1f8098e3a109d766aef554389f363c83.gif[/img]

We think the most interesting aspect of this style is the parallax effect it creates. (Parallax is the visual effect of close objects appearing to move quickly while more distant objects move more slowly.) Just imagine driving in a car and close trees move quickly while far trees seem to barely move, and you get the idea.

The new-look also allows you to ‘peek’ around objects, so we’ve had to adjust some of the art to match.
This is because we’ve converted our orthographic camera to a perspective camera. This allows it to behave like a real-life camera and has a Field of View - In real-life cameras are never perfectly flat and have a slight curvature, so objects at the side of the screen are angled while objects in the centre are head-on.

We’re hard at work making the game look and feel as good as possible, so if you think the new look is an improvement let us know!

notes.title: Developer's Blog - Behind the Art
notes.content:
[b]Hey Everyone! [/b]

Welcome to our first Developer blog for Monster Harvest! On the run up to launch we’ll be looking to post these blogs regularly. They’ll cover things such as challenges we faced; things we think you may just find of interest as well as the triumphs we’ve achieved! 

If there’s anything in particular you’re interested in finding out though - jump in the comments and let us know! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/579cb4c99525af5ddd056e67b58776a0b7cfdf84.gif[/img]

This week we thought we would kick off with what inspired us to make Monster Harvest in pixel art. Games from the 90’s hold some very fond memories for everyone on the team here at Maple Powered Games. Even if we all forget the limitations that era had...! With the 8-bit world of the 90’s being held in glorious nostalgia and firmly at the front of our minds, when setting out to create Monster Harvest, we knew there was only one art style we wanted to create. Our job now was to thread the metaphorical needle and deliver pixel art, but with a modern feel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/e282effce4fbd9550ccdc91cd12da9f22ee08d0c.gif[/img]

There are two competing ways to create modern pixel art though - Pixel Purism and Hi-Bit:
Pixel Purism is, in our view, an attempt to replicate the technical artistic limitations of older consoles and deliver as similar a visual experience. Usually only minor compromises are made, such as with the game Shovel Knight, which increased to a more realistic 16 colour palette to allow for more skin tones for characters. Other common changes usually include modern widescreen formatting and more subtle things like parallax scrolling.

For Monster Harvest we opted to lean further towards the Hi-Bit technique, a term coined by the developers of OwlBoy, D-Pad Studios. Hi-Bit allows the game to have no restriction on colour palette and uses a large number of shadow effects, lighting effects, and some post processing in order to achieve its style. So… I suppose you could say we were going for beauty over authenticity. But we think it paid off!

Monster Harvest is built in Unity so it’s not purely a 2D game. Instead, it’s a 3D render with the camera locked to a 90-degree angle aiming at the world. The camera is also orthographic and pixel perfect - meaning there's no camera lensing and a post process effect operates to correct any unforeseen errors that may arise. This has a lot of benefits but… also some limitations as well.

Overall, to ensure we’re creating our artistic vision to the best of our ability it’s important to be following a style guide. The style guide for Monster Harvest is pretty extensive but ultimately it focuses on extreme attention to detail and (here's a big one) non-repeating tiles. Pixel art games of the past were limited to using a few basic tiles to build their worlds, but we certainly aren't - so we find that adding as much variety as possible really seems to make the game stand out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38633059/4570d744ea4de04086b6ba337202be95c86fa60f.gif[/img]

The art in the game has changed a lot since our announcement and the screenshots you can see on the Steam store page. We’ve been defining it and ensuring it’s really our own. 

But what does everyone think? Does our super-saturated pixel artwork hit the nail on the head? Does anything stick out? Let us know your thoughts. ːsteamhappyː
